summary: A 1931 L-4 cab on Hidden Lake Peak, staffed until 1958, then saved from abandonment in 1961 by a volunteer club and still used as an emergency hiking shelter.

access.note: Reachable by trail in the Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest; used as an emergency hiking shelter, not an active fire lookout.

visit.trail_note: Popular hiking summit near North Cascades National Park.

events.note: Gable-roof L-4 cab built by Larsen Bros. Construction atop Hidden Lake Peak.
Staffing ended when the Forest Service closed many north Cascades lookouts.
Dr. Fred Darvill and the Skagit Alpine Club obtained a special-use permit to restore and maintain the structure.
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places (significant year 1931 per nomination).
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, July 9, 1996.

evidence.quote: The gable roof L-4 groundhouse lookout built by the U.S. Forest Service atop Hidden Lake Peak in 1931 was staffed until 1958 when many lookouts in the north Cascades were closed.

evidence.supports: 1961 restoration by Darvill and Skagit Alpine Club
evidence.quote: In 1961 Dr. Fred Darvill and the Skagit Alpine Club obtained a special use permit to restore and maintain the scenic historic structure which is popular with hikers.

evidence.supports: Builder Larsen Bros. Construction, significant year 1931
Built 1931, last staffed 1950s, now an emergency shelter
evidence.quote: Built in 1931, this gable-roofed L-4 cab was last staffed in the 1950's. It is presently maintained as an emergency hiking shelter, and is listed on the National Historic Lookout Register.

evidence.supports: Nearby Anderson Butte lookout removed in 1964, contrast case

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR says staffed until 1958; firelookout.com says last staffed in the 1950s, which is consistent but less precise. Used the more specific NHLR date.

sources.title: National Register of Historic Places nomination/asset detail, NRIS 87001184
Anderson Butte Trail 611.1
sources.publisher: USDA Forest Service - Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest

notes_for_editor: NHLR page lists the lookout as 'Available for Rental,' but this looks like it may be a generic NHLR field rather than confirmed current rental booking info; I described it cautiously as an emergency shelter and flagged the discrepancy in the story rather than asserting a formal rental program. Did not find a source giving an exact NRHP listing date beyond the significant year 1931; AssetDetail page text was truncated so the listing year is inferred, worth double-checking directly against the full nomination PDF if available.
